Hi, we're team BTYECODE, and this is Paradox, our entry for the Fraud Prevention and Security track. In a B2B travel platform, the bugs that cost real money don't look like bugs: a refund paid twice, a fare set by the agent, one agency reading another's passports. All of them return 200 OK. Scanners look for bad inputs; Paradox looks for outcomes that should be impossible.

Here's a real finding from our prototype. Book, pay, cancel, then cancel again: every reply is 200 OK, yet the agency's wallet gains 7,776 rupees each time. Paradox catches it because it checks rules every correct platform keeps, not attack signatures. It measures every money bug in rupees on a shadow ledger, plants canary data so leaks prove themselves, replays every bug three times and shrinks it to a minimal proof, and learns the platform with no API docs. Along the bottom is the full agent loop from the problem statement, all eight stages built and tested: detect change, learn and build the inventory, plan, execute safely, verify, triage, report and retest.

And it already works. Across 22 runs with randomly planted bugs it found all 172 with zero false alarms; a signature scanner on the same inputs found 51 and missed every money and cross-agency bug. On an airline platform it was never built for, it found all seven bugs after two small general fixes. A new deploy is checked within seconds. On the right are the adoption risks a security team would raise, and how each one is handled in code. Roll-out is simple: point it at staging on day one, run it on every deploy in week one, and gate releases in CI in week two.
